Subject: Request: VM evidence + SLA attestation for SIG/SOC2 review

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this on. Our SOC2 auditor has asked for a consolidated VM evidence packet covering: scan cadence details (authenticated vs unauthenticated), historical scan artifacts for the last 90 days, CVE remediation SLAs (by severity), and a short attestation we can provide to auditors that the timelines below are Redwood policy for hosted customers.

Specifically we need:
- A short paragraph describing scan cadence and ownership (who runs weekly scans vs monthly authenticated)
- SLA commitments (Critical/High/Medium) including any escalation timeline and fallback model (e.g., fallback to queued patches when immediate remediation not possible)
- Sample artifact: last authenticated scan export (prefer CSV/JSON) and a patch manifest showing CVE -> owner -> fix deployed date
- An attestation letter we can sign and include in our SIG/SOC2 evidence binder

Can you get this to me by end-of-day Tuesday (COB 9/16)? If you have a draft attestation we can kick it back with minor edits, that would be ideal.

Attached: SIG_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (we highlighted the VM tabs).

Thanks,
Mike

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Mike Collins <mike.collins@finlender.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + SLA attestation for SIG/SOC2 review

Mike —

Thanks for the clarity and the deadline. Below is a concise summary and I've attached an evidence index and a draft attestation PDF for your review. We can sign the attestation once you confirm the final wording.

Summary (quick):
- Scan cadence: automated unauthenticated scans across internet-exposed assets run nightly; authenticated credentialed scans against internal images run weekly. Monthly full authenticated scans run on the 1st of each month against prod images and an on-demand run is triggered for any major infra change.
- Remediation SLA (standard policy):
  - Critical (CVSS >=9.0 or actively exploited): remediate or deploy compensating control within 7 calendar days; immediate incident escalation to on-call and Dedicated capacity review.
  - High (CVSS 7.0-8.9): remediate within 30 calendar days; patch window prioritized in next sprint if no immediate patch available.
  - Medium (CVSS 4.0-6.9): remediate within 90 calendar days, tracked on backlog with mitigations documented.
- Exception handling: documented exception requests for legacy/third-party libs require compensating controls and are timeboxed; exceptions are visible in the patch manifest and require VP-level approval.

Evidence included in the drive link and attached index:
- redwood_vm_evidence_index.csv (index of exports below)
- scan-results-20250901-20250907.zip (authenticated scan exports, sample)
- patch_manifest.pdf (CVE -> owner -> mitigation -> deployment date)
- attestation_draft_finlender.pdf (draft attestation for your SIG/SOC2 binder)

Quick notes on process:
- We retain monthly authenticated scans and patch manifests for 18 months for compliance customers; raw scan archives (full exports) are retained for 90 days (we provide extracts on request).
- For hosted customers on Dedicated, we can offer extended retention or a transfer of raw artifacts under an NDA.

If the SLA tiers above are acceptable, confirm and we will sign the attached attestation; Ben is copied to add any additional artifacts (ticket IDs, change windows).

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood_vm_evidence_index.csv (text/csv), attestation_draft_finlender.pdf (pdf), scan-results-20250901-20250907.zip (zip)

Mike / Jonas —

Following up with the technical artifacts you asked for and a few clarifying details for the auditor:

1) Evidence location (read-only, expiring): https://s3.redwood.internal/finlender/vm-evidence/2025-09 (presigned link included in related_links)
2) Contents of scan-results-20250901-20250907.zip: authenticated-scan-full.json, filtered-vuln-list.csv, remediation-ticket-IDs.csv
3) SIEM integration: Vulnerability findings are ingested into our central SIEM (Splunk) with a UUID per finding; we maintain linkage between vuln-findings -> Jira ticket -> deployment pipeline. Time-to-fix is therefore traceable to commit and CI/CD deployment timestamps.
4) Patch manifest note: in the attached remediation_playbook we map CVE -> owner -> PR link -> deployment pipeline job ID. If auditors need PR hashes/CI logs we can provide them under an NDA.

On exceptions: I want to underline that for some third-party compiled dependencies we offer compensating controls (runtime mitigations) when patching would cause unacceptable customer impact. Those compensating controls include WAF rules, feature flags to disable vulnerable component, and runtime monitoring alarms. All exceptions are timeboxed and listed in the patch manifest PDF.

I've also attached a short change log excerpt so the auditor can see a sample of tickets closed within the High bucket for Aug-Sep.

Ben Carter
Security Ops
Redwood Inference
